mechanism: Section 179D Energy Efficient Commercial Buildings Deduction
statute_or_program: 26 U.S.C. 179D; amended by One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), P.L. 119-21, sec. 70020, signed 7/4/2025, adding new subsection 179D(i)
status_2026_09: Active but sunsetting. Deduction is DISALLOWED for any property whose CONSTRUCTION BEGINS after June 30, 2026 (confirmed via 26 USC 179D(i) statutory text). This is a construction-start cutoff, not a placed-in-service cutoff — a project that begins construction on or before 6/30/2026 stays eligible even if completed years later.
key_dates: OBBBA signed 7/4/2025 | Statutory cutoff: construction must begin on or before 6/30/2026 | Property must otherwise meet the existing >=25% whole-building energy-cost-savings threshold vs ASHRAE 90.1 baseline | No sunset previously existed (179D was made permanent by the 2020 Consolidated Appropriations Act before OBBBA added this termination)
value: 2025 inflation-adjusted deduction: $0.58-$1.16/sq ft without prevailing wage & apprenticeship (scales $0.02/sqft per % point of savings above 25%, capped at 50% savings); $2.90-$5.81/sq ft WITH prevailing wage & registered apprenticeship (scales $0.12/sqft per % point, 5x multiplier). Eligible systems: interior lighting, HVAC, service hot water, building envelope. 2026-specific inflation-adjusted dollar figures were not independently located this session (IRS had not published a distinct 2026 Rev. Proc. figure we could confirm) — verify current-year number at irs.gov/energy.gov before quoting to a customer.
sector: commercial (all EP customer types: QSR, retail, hotel, distribution, light industrial, ag)
action_for_ep: A retrofit that begins construction in October 2026 is INELIGIBLE for 179D — construction starts three months after the statutory cutoff. Do not offer 179D as an incentive for any EP project starting construction after 6/30/2026. For deals in the pipeline now, push customers to formally 'begin construction' (physical work test or 5% safe-harbor equivalent under 179D case law/guidance) before 6/30/2026 to lock in eligibility even if installation finishes later. Stacking with a utility rebate is generally fine since 179D is a federal tax deduction and utility rebates are a separate cash/bill-credit mechanism, but the utility rebate can affect the customer's depreciable basis or taxable income depending on rebate structure — flag for the customer's CPA rather than asserting stackability outright. For the rare EP customer that is a government or tax-exempt entity, 179D can be ALLOCATED to the designer/contractor (a third-party payment mechanism) instead of the owner — worth checking if any EP customers are municipally or nonprofit owned.

mechanism: Section 48 Energy Credit — Geothermal Heat Pump Property
statute_or_program: 26 U.S.C. 48(a); OBBBA did not accelerate this technology's schedule
status_2026_09: Active, long runway, EXPLICITLY excluded from OBBBA's wind/solar acceleration. Applies ONLY to ground/water-source (geothermal) heat pump property — does NOT cover air-source heat-pump rooftop units (RTUs).
key_dates: Construction must begin before 1/1/2035 to be eligible at all | Base 6% / bonus 30% (with prevailing wage & apprenticeship) of eligible basis for construction beginning through 2032 | steps down to 5.2%/26% in 2033, 4.4%/22% in 2034, $0 after 2034 construction starts
value: 6% base credit, up to 30% with prevailing wage and registered apprenticeship compliance, of eligible cost basis of true geothermal (ground/water-source) heat pump equipment.
action_for_ep: IMPORTANT CORRECTION FOR SALES MESSAGING: EP's 'heat-pump RTU' offering is an AIR-SOURCE packaged rooftop unit, not a geothermal (ground/water-source) system. It does NOT qualify for this geothermal ITC. Do not let sales reps imply a heat-pump RTU install earns the 30% geothermal tax credit — this is a common and costly mix-up. This credit is only relevant to EP if EP ever adds true ground-source geothermal heat pumps to its measure list.

mechanism: Section 48 / 48E — Solar Thermal, Solar Process Heat, Solar Water Heating Property
statute_or_program: 26 U.S.C. 48 (legacy 'solar energy property' definition) vs. 26 U.S.C. 48E (technology-neutral 'Clean Electricity Investment Credit')
status_2026_09: UNCLEAR — see explanation. Legacy Section 48 explicitly lists equipment that heats/cools a structure or provides hot water or solar process heat as eligible 'solar energy property,' but for most technologies (solar included) Section 48's technology-specific rules generally require construction to have BEGUN BEFORE 1/1/2025 (the geothermal-heat-pump carveout to 2035 is a named exception; solar was not similarly carved out). New projects starting construction in 2025 or later are expected to use the replacement Section 48E credit instead — but 48E is statutorily framed as the 'Clean Electricity Investment Credit,' requiring the qualified facility to PRODUCE ELECTRICITY with a greenhouse-gas emissions rate of zero or less. Non-electric solar thermal/process-heat/water-heating equipment does not produce electricity, so whether it has ANY current federal ITC pathway is genuinely unresolved from the sources reviewed this session — secondary sources conflict (some list 'Solar Water Heat/Solar Space Heat/Solar Thermal Process Heat' as 48-eligible technologies without noting the 2025 construction-start cutoff; one source stated 48E disallows credit for 'qualified solar water heating expenditures' after 7/4/2025, which may actually be describing a residential/25D-adjacent provision, not a commercial 48E rule).
key_dates: Section 48 (legacy): construction generally must have begun before 1/1/2025 for solar technologies | Section 48E: in effect for facilities placed in service after 1/1/2025, framed around electricity generation | Could not confirm a specific commercial-solar-thermal cutoff date from primary statutory text this session
value: Not published — do not quote a specific ITC percentage for solar thermal without independent tax-counsel confirmation. If a pre-2025 legacy Section 48 pathway somehow still applies: 6% base / up to 30% with prevailing wage+apprenticeship. If no 48E pathway exists for non-electric solar equipment: $0 federal ITC for new solar-thermal construction in 2025 or later.
action_for_ep: HIGH-PRIORITY OPEN ITEM: this is the single most consequential unresolved question in this deliverable for EP's solar_thermal measure. Before including any ITC percentage for solar thermal in a proposal, EP should get a written opinion from a tax attorney or CPA who specializes in energy credits (or call an IRS practitioner line) confirming whether commercial solar water heating / process heat property has a live 2026 federal ITC path under 48 or 48E. Until then, market solar thermal on utility rebates, depreciation, and operating-cost savings only — not on an ITC percentage.

mechanism: Section 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit (solar PV / storage / other electricity-generating tech)
statute_or_program: 26 U.S.C. 48E, as amended by OBBBA sec. 70512
status_2026_09: Active for non-wind/solar tech through 2032 at 100%, phasing down 2033-2035; wind & solar specifically accelerated — must begin construction by 7/4/2026 or be placed in service by 12/31/2027. Not directly relevant to EP's current measure list (EP's 'solar thermal' is non-electric; EP does not sell PV).
key_dates: OBBBA signed 7/4/2025 | Wind/solar: construction must begin by 7/4/2026, OR placed in service by 12/31/2027 if construction begins after that date | Projects beginning construction on/before 7/4/2026 get a 4-year completion safe harbor (generally through 12/31/2030) | FEOC 'material assistance' cost-ratio test applies to facilities beginning construction after 12/31/2025, ramping from 40% non-FEOC content in 2026 up to 60% by 2030 for solar | Non-wind/solar tech (storage, fuel cells, CHP-adjacent categories under 48E) phases 100%/75%/50%/0% for construction beginning 2033/2034/2035/2036+
value: Base 6% / bonus 30% with prevailing wage & apprenticeship, of qualified investment; domestic-content bonus adder 10% (rates step up through 2026-2027); FEOC-compliant sourcing required for full value from 2026 onward.
action_for_ep: Not currently applicable to EP's measure list since EP does not install solar PV or battery storage. Flag only if EP expands into on-site solar electric or thermal-energy-storage-as-a-service offerings — in that case the 7/4/2026 construction-start deadline (already passed as of this report if a project has not yet started) is the operative constraint for full-value solar PV credits.

status_2026_09: Active for non-wind/solar generators through 2032 with phase-down thereafter; wind/solar accelerated on the same 7/4/2026 construction-start / 12/31/2027 placed-in-service schedule as 48E. Not relevant to EP.
key_dates: OBBBA signed 7/4/2025 | Wind/solar termination for facilities placed in service after 12/31/2027 if construction begins after 7/4/2026 | FEOC restrictions apply from 2026 (no 'specified foreign entity' or 'foreign-influenced entity' may claim the credit)
value: Per-kWh production credit, inflation-adjusted annually (2026 factor published in Federal Register 9/4/2026); not meaningful for a company that does not generate/sell electricity.
action_for_ep: Not applicable — EP does not operate as an electricity generator/producer. Included only to confirm this mechanism does not touch any current EP measure.

mechanism: MACRS Bonus Depreciation (100%) and Section 179 Expensing
statute_or_program: 26 U.S.C. 168(k), permanently restored to 100% by OBBBA sec. 70301; IRS Notice 2026-11 (1/14/2026)
status_2026_09: ACTIVE and, per IRS, the single most broadly usable federal mechanism for EP's whole measure list. 100% bonus depreciation is PERMANENT (no longer phasing down) for qualified property acquired after 1/19/2025 and placed in service after that date.
key_dates: OBBBA signed 7/4/2025 | 100% bonus depreciation applies to qualified property ACQUIRED after 1/19/2025 (property under binding contract before 1/19/2025 does NOT get the restored 100% rate even if placed in service later — it follows the old phase-down: 40% for 2025 placed-in-service, 20% for 2026, 0% after) | IRS Notice 2026-11 (issued 1/14/2026) is the primary transition guidance | Section 179 expensing cap was also increased by OBBBA but the exact new dollar cap/phase-out threshold was NOT independently confirmed via a primary IRS source this session — verify current Sec. 179 limits at irs.gov/pub 946 before quoting a figure to a customer.
value: 100% first-year bonus depreciation for qualifying MACRS property with a class life <=20 years, including most equipment. CLASSIFICATION NUANCE THAT MATTERS MOST FOR EP: a rooftop HVAC unit that becomes a structural component of the building is generally 39-year nonresidential real property and does NOT independently get bonus depreciation; controls/sensor/VFD retrofit equipment that is add-on personal property (not a structural component) is typically 5-7 year MACRS property and DOES qualify for 100% bonus depreciation; interior HVAC/controls work done as an improvement to an existing nonresidential building's interior may separately qualify as Qualified Improvement Property (QIP), a 15-year class life that also qualifies for 100% bonus depreciation (QIP explicitly excludes building enlargements, elevators/escalators, and internal structural framework, but does not exclude HVAC on its face — however, exterior/rooftop-mounted equipment is commonly treated as a structural component rather than an 'interior' improvement in practice). This 39-year vs 15-year(QIP) vs 5-7-year(personal property) line is exactly why cost segregation studies exist, and we could not get authoritative primary-source confirmation this session of how EP's specific optimizer/CryoGenX4/RTU packages would be classified by an IRS examiner — recommend EP have a cost-segregation specialist classify a representative project.
action_for_ep: This is likely EP's highest-value, most durable federal talking point post-OBBBA: 100% bonus depreciation is now PERMANENT, unlike the pre-OBBBA phase-down to 0% by 2027. For controls/optimizer retrofits (add-on equipment, not structural), EP can credibly tell customers 'the full cost is depreciable in year one.' For RTU replacements (structural HVAC), the classification is murkier — do not promise 100% first-year write-off without a cost-segregation opinion; RTUs replacing existing structural HVAC may default to 39-year treatment absent a QIP or personal-property argument. Utility rebates generally reduce the depreciable basis of the equipment (the rebate is typically treated as a reduction in cost, not taxable income, under general tax principles for a capital cost rebate) — so bonus depreciation is 'stackable' with a utility rebate only in the sense that depreciation applies to the NET (post-rebate) cost; flag this basis-reduction mechanic to the customer's CPA rather than promising the two benefits are fully additive on the gross project cost.

mechanism: USDA REAP — Renewable Energy System & Energy Efficiency Improvement GRANTS
statute_or_program: 7 U.S.C. 8107 (Rural Energy for America Program), 7 CFR 4280 Subpart B; Executive Order 14315 'Ending Market-Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign Controlled Energy Sources'
status_2026_09: PAUSED as of this writing. USDA Rural Business-Cooperative Service halted ALL REAP grant awards (both the energy-efficiency-improvement category and the renewable-energy-system category, which would include solar thermal) effective 3/31/2026, pending a rulemaking to amend 7 CFR 4280 Subpart B for consistency with EO 14315. USDA said it will issue a NEW Notice of Funding Opportunity once the rule is final, and that prior applicants may reapply; we could not confirm via primary source whether the new NOFO had been issued as of 9/22/2026 (WebSearch budget exhausted before this could be re-checked — treat as 'still paused, verify with State Energy Coordinator' pending direct confirmation).
key_dates: Grants originally: up to 50% of eligible project cost, max $500,000 for energy-efficiency-improvement grants and max $1,000,000 for renewable-energy-system grants (post-IRA increase from $250k/$500k) | Grant pause announced/effective 3/31/2026 | No confirmed reopening date as of 9/22/2026
value: Historically up to 50% grant of eligible project cost (subject to the $500k EE / $1M RE caps above). Currently $0 available while paused — cannot be relied upon for active proposals until a new NOFO issues.
sector: commercial — RESTRICTED to rural areas (population <=50,000) AND to either an agricultural producer (>=50% of gross income from agricultural operations) or a 'rural small business' meeting SBA size standards. Excludes most of EP's non-rural QSR/retail/hotel/distribution customers.
action_for_ep: Two-part impact: (1) Do NOT include REAP grant dollars in any active EP proposal right now — the grant program is paused with no confirmed reopening date; this could strand a deal if quoted as a funding source. (2) Even when REAP reopens, it only helps the subset of EP's rural agricultural and rural-small-business customers, not EP's broader QSR/retail/hotel/distribution book, which is mostly not in qualifying rural areas. An energy audit or ASABE/AEE-certified energy assessment is required as part of the application for the efficiency-improvement category — factor that lead time in if/when the program reopens.

statute_or_program: 7 U.S.C. 8107; 7 CFR 4280 Subpart B (loan guarantee provisions)
status_2026_09: ACTIVE. USDA explicitly stated the guaranteed-loan side of REAP continues to accept applications even while the grant side is paused.
key_dates: Grant pause (3/31/2026) explicitly did NOT extend to guaranteed loans, per USDA's own announcement
value: Loan guarantee percentage and maximum loan amount were not independently confirmed via a primary rd.usda.gov source this session (the official program pages returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch); historically REAP guarantees a large majority of loan principal up to a multi-million-dollar cap — verify exact current percentage/cap directly with a USDA Rural Development state office before quoting to a customer.

mechanism: SBA 504 Green Loan Program (Energy Public Policy Project)
statute_or_program: 13 CFR 120.882 (SBA 504/CDC loan program, Green/Energy Public Policy goal)
status_2026_09: ACTIVE, no rural restriction — broader applicability than REAP for EP's commercial book.
key_dates: No OBBBA-related change identified for this SBA loan program in this session's research
value: Qualifies for expanded/second/third 504 loan(s) if the project reduces energy consumption or energy use intensity (EUI) by at least 10% compared to historical use through building upgrades (equipment or systems). Raises the SBA maximum contribution to a $5.5M cap per loan (vs. $5M standard) and allows an aggregate outstanding SBA 504 balance up to $16.5M across up to three green-energy loans (vs. $5.5M standard aggregate cap).
sector: commercial (nationwide, no rural restriction — fits EP's QSR/retail/hotel/distribution/light-industrial customers better than REAP)
action_for_ep: Good fit for EP's non-rural commercial customers that REAP can't reach. A bundled optimizer + RTU replacement + thermal-barrier-coating project that documents a >=10% EUI reduction (an energy audit/M&V report showing this should be a deliverable EP already produces) can unlock a larger, cheaper SBA 504 loan for the customer — worth building '10% EUI reduction' into EP's standard savings-modeling output as a named qualifying threshold for sales conversations.

mechanism: FERC Order No. 2222 — Wholesale Market Participation of Distributed Energy Resource Aggregations
statute_or_program: FERC Order No. 2222 (issued 9/17/2020); RTO/ISO compliance filings ongoing
status_2026_09: Context row, not a direct EP revenue mechanism today. Implementation remains slow nationally (PJM, NYISO, SPP progressing compliance filings as of a Jan. 2026 tracker report; capacity-market DER participation timeline targets 2027-2028). CRITICAL LOCAL NOTE: South Carolina is NOT inside an RTO/ISO footprint that FERC directly regulates for retail dispatch — Duke Energy Carolinas/Progress and Dominion/Santee Cooper territory in SC is vertically-integrated utility territory, not an organized wholesale market region, so Order 2222's DER-aggregator wholesale-market access has little to no direct near-term applicability to EP's home-state customers absent SC joining an RTO or a market like SEEM maturing into something FERC-jurisdictional.
key_dates: Order issued 9/17/2020 | RTO/ISO compliance filings ongoing through 2026 | Capacity-market DER aggregation participation targeted for the 2028/2029 delivery year (auction ~5/2026) in at least one RTO | Not independently confirmed whether SC is covered by any FERC-jurisdictional wholesale market as of 9/2026
value: No direct dollar value — it is a market-access rule enabling aggregators (a third party, not the building owner) to bundle customer curtailment/flexibility and sell it into wholesale energy/capacity/ancillary markets, where such markets exist and allow it.
sector: wholesale electricity market (context — pays an AGGREGATOR/third party, not the building owner directly)
action_for_ep: Do not build a demand-response revenue projection into an SC-based EP proposal on the strength of Order 2222 — SC customers are very likely outside any FERC-jurisdictional RTO footprint today, so there's no live wholesale market for an aggregator to sell EP-enabled curtailment into locally. This becomes relevant only (a) for EP customers with facilities in RTO territory (PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP/ISO-NE/ERCOT-adjacent states), or (b) if/when a Southeast market (e.g., SEEM) evolves into a FERC-jurisdictional structure DER aggregators can access. Revisit this row if EP expands outside SC/Duke/Dominion/Santee Cooper territory.
